To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the frequency domain representation of asymmetry is an effective way to capture the facial dynamics of human subjects; 2) the use of HMMs to capture the dynamics of the asymmetry representation is effective; 3) the use of the HMM-based asymmetry representation for face identification from video is significantly better than using still images.

(1) The HMM-based method for human face identification using frequency domain asymmetry representation performs much better than IPCA-based identification, and (2) The HMMs trained with frequency domain asymmetry representations of the training video data can effectively capture the dynamic characteristics of the video sequences and can be used to identify the test subjects.

the proposed method can achieve a significant performance improvement in human face identification from video data by exploiting the frequency domain representation of temporal facial asymmetry dynamics.

we have developed a novel human face recognition scheme from videos based on a novel frequency domain representation of the facial asymmetry and a HMM-based classification scheme, which is shown to be much better than the still image-based methods in the same scenario.
the HMM based approach outperforms the IPCA approach by more than 30%, and that the HMM approach is also more robust to illumination and expression variations.

the temporal information of the facial expression is very important and can significantly improve the face identification performance.
